title: A Letter from Kolvar

narrative.text: Kolvar's reply is on heavy stationery, his name embossed at the top in dark ink. The letter is brief — Kolvar does not waste words. But it is not hostile. It is the letter of a man who has been invited to negotiate and is considering the invitation.

Chancellor. Your letter was... unexpected. I have grown accustomed to public confrontation with your government. A private communication suggests a different approach. I am willing to discuss terms. Not because I trust you — but because I believe you have finally understood that governing requires more than conviction. It requires the ability to make deals with people you would rather not share a room with. My parliamentary secretary will arrange the details.

monologue: He used the word 'unexpected.' From Kolvar, that is practically a compliment. He is offering a ceasefire, not an alliance. But a ceasefire is more than I had this morning. The constitution needs his votes. The question is what he wants in return — and whether I can afford to give it.

choices.text: "He is willing to talk. That is more than I expected. It is not peace — Kolvar and I will never have peace. But it is a ceasefire. For now, that may be enough to keep the government alive."

reactions.text: He does not respond — the letter was his message. But his parliamentary secretary calls within the hour. The meeting will be scheduled. In his office. On his terms. He understands the concession.
